back: A past action or situation linked to now, with no finished time stated: *She has lost her key* (it is still lost).
notes: Used with since, for, already, yet, just, ever, never; not with yesterday or last week.

back: The earlier of two past actions: *The film had started when we arrived.*
The longer background action takes the past continuous; the short interrupting action takes the past simple: *I was sleeping when the phone rang.*
The base form: *Did you see? She doesn't know.*
The past participle: *has written, have gone, had begun, has rung.*
After when, as soon as, before, after, until and if, use a present tense for the future: *I'll tell him when he arrives.*
lie (rest): lie, lay, lain. lay (put down): lay, laid, laid. lie (tell untruths): lie, lied, lied.
begin, began, begun; ring, rang, rung; swim, swam, swum; drink, drank, drunk; write, wrote, written; seek, sought, sought.
Keep the verbs in a passage in the same time frame; move back to the past perfect only for an earlier event.
notes: Check a story by reading only the verbs.

back: An action that will be completed before a time in the future: *By June we will have finished the syllabus.*
